To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
genetic polymorphisms of genes that are linked to bone disease are associated with bone disease in myloma.
we have discovered a genetic signature of myeloma patients with bone disease that includes SNPs in EPHX1 and Gsk3beta, as well as myeloma cell levels of DKK-1 and serum LDH.

we identified genetic markers that are associated with the presence of myeloma in the bone, the severity of myeloma-related bone disease, myeloma cell levels of the protein DKK1, and the survival of myeloma patients.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of genetic polymorphrphisms associated with bone disease in multiple myeloma.
identifying genetic markers that are linked to myeloma bone lesions, and that may also predict response to therapy.
the identification of genetic polymorphrphisms associated with bone disease in myelaoma.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
genetic polymorphisms of GSK-3β, EPHX1 and TNFSF-8 and myelomal cell DKK- 1 expression levels are linked to bone disease and patient outcome in myeloma.
the SNPs in EPHX1 and GSK3B are linked to bone disease, but that these SNPs are not linked to DKK-1 levels.
the genetic polymorphisms of the genes EPHX1 and Gsk3b are linked to bone disease, and that DKK-1, EPHX1 polymorphisms, Gsk3b polymorphism, TNFSF polymorphism and LDH are linked to bone lesions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

genetic polymorphisms in EPHX1 and GSK3β are associated with bone disease in myelaoma and that these polymorphisms can be utilized to predict the number of bone lytic lesions, DKK-1 levels, and survival.
the genetic polymorphisms identified in our study are associated with myeloma bone lesions, and may have utility in prognostication and in the development of new therapeutics.

the EPHX1 SNP rs1051740 was associated with myeloma bone lesions, log 2 DKK- 1 expression and patient survival, and was a significant independent prognostic factor in multivariate regression analysis.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the genetic polymorphisms identified here are linked to bone disease and that the SNPs in EPHX1 and Gsk3beta are associated with the expression levels of DKK-1, a key myeloma cell protein involved in the pathogenesis of bone disease.
the EPHX1 gene is a major contributor to bone disease in multiple myeloma.
the bone disease of multiple myeloma is a multifactorial disease that is driven in part by the genetic makeup of the patient.
